part.text: {"items":[{"index":1,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"NA","quote":"fix a 16–24 molecule panel spanning hydrocarbons and esters, and spend the compute on a force-field/parameterization axis instead ... each new run now tests a different error floor rather than re-sampling the same one","reason":"Compute shifts from more molecules under one force field to varying parameterizations; each run tests a different error floor, buying new information."},{"index":2,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"NA","quote":"Change the measured quantity: compute self-diffusion coefficient D from mean-squared displacement, a single-particle average that converges roughly an order of magnitude faster than Green–Kubo stress integrals, and rank molecules by a diffusion–viscosity scaling relation","reason":"Swaps Green–Kubo viscosity for faster-converging diffusion D with a scaling relation, so compute buys 5–10× more ranked molecules, not noise reduction."},{"index":3,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"NA","quote":"Change the unit of work to a chemistry-class correction parameter and the objective to the learning curve of a class-conditional bias model (multiplicative correction per class with a chain-length slope).","reason":"Changes measured objective from independent per-molecule error to a class-bias learning curve; compute buys shared calibration and a how-few-suffice decision."}]}
